title: Typography
description: Edited in the /type lab (development only); npm run tokens turns it into --type-* custom properties in _type.generated.css. Sizes and line-heights are px. 'small' is the setting below the breakpoint, 'large' the one above it. The breakpoint is the text-column width where the large setting takes over, applied as a viewport min-width. mode 'stepped' switches at the breakpoint; 'fluid' grows from viewports.min and stops at the breakpoint. The scale starts from Chimero's 18/24 and 20/28 and hasn't been tested yet. The playground carries no brand of its own, so the faces are the ones already on the machine and the sample copy is filler: a site replaces both with its client's.

sample.title: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
sample.text: This paragraph exists to be read at length rather than admired in isolation, because a typeface only shows its character once the eye has somewhere to travel. Watch what happens to the rhythm of the line as the measure changes, where the word spacing opens up, and whether the descenders of one line crowd the capitals of the next. Numerals like 1853 and 2026 are worth a look too, as are the shapes that tend to give a face away: a lowercase g, a capital R, a question mark. Replace this with the client's own writing as soon as there is any, because real sentences break in places that filler never does.
